title: What a drummer should do: two hands, sock cymbal, back beat
summary: Ridgley criticizes his present mechanical drummer and says a drummer needs two good hands, the 6/8 rhythm and the back beat.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What is that thing that the drummers have in New Orleans?
You know what, what is it?
Can you define it? What makes it so special?

You know, really, I don't know. We've always, we've always, I think it, I think it's from, because we play, we have this Dixieland thing. You know, while he got the new name for it, but I still call it Dixieland because they're all the same thing. But I think it stems from that in our parade thing. You know, this, you think, boom, boom, boom, boom, syncopated, you know, and this falls right into a drummer, you know, directing in a band. And he got to have this feeling kind of thing. And if, you know, you can be mechanical. Now, there are also mechanical drummers. I had one playing with me, and my present drummer is mechanical in this respect. First of all, he had one hand, his left hand ain't worth a darn. You got to tell him what to do with his left hand, and then he can do it a little while, then it really slacks off. Uh-huh. His, the sock cymbal, you know, a drummer's supposed to know what that sock cymbal is there for. See, the new drummers, there's something else, you know. Being a band leader, I know all these things. The drummers today, the only time they use their sock cymbal is when they just lighten up on it to open it a little bit, just get a little ring. Other than that, they just have it there and keep their foot on it and keep it closed, play it a little open. But they, see, that's the drummer. Boy, you hear that sock cymbal working. And you check this now. You check these new drummers. They don't know nothing about sock cymbal. Uh-huh. They don't know what is there. All they know is there.
What should a, what is your feeling? What should a drummer be doing? That, well, a drummer. To support your music.

Well, well, well. What should a drummer be doing? First of all, he got to have two good hands. Uh-huh. See, because you need the solid back beat thing. You need the 6-8 rhythm. So these are two things that got to be going together. Uh-huh. Okay. Uh, if he ain't got but one hand, naturally, he ain't gonna play most likely the 6-8 because that's where it comes from that left hand. He might have, he might, now my drummer cannot play the back beat. I told him last night. I said, man, you play the back beat like as if you're hitting on a paper bag with some A in it and you're afraid you might bust it. I said, man, play the back beat. I said, let him play the car. You know, because this would make it effective. Can't do this. Well, but, and he'll say, man, that's before my time. And I, sometimes I feel like, man, well, look, you just pack up and leave. And the reason I just don't dissolve it is because it just got, it's hard finding people today. And I said, man, I got three people in my band I could fire right now. Right. Just like you. You know, because I know, I know, and I go along with it. But if I can get anything going, if I can get any kind of work where I get some work, I go in a hotel for three, six months, I have, I have the best band time because I get rid of all these nothing players, right, just quick. I keep them because I ain't got nothing to myself.
